name: Rheon Systems CorpSec Field Loadout MK-6
description:
Head-to-toe tactical rig issued to mid-tier CorpSec units. Matte-black segmented TacShell torso armor over a moisture-wicking graphene underlayer, ballistic-rated ceramic shoulder pauldrons, and articulated knee-strike greaves. Helmet is a low-profile carbon composite with integrated HUD visor and neural uplink port at the occipital ridge. Gloves are cut-resistant syntex with haptic feedback nodes at the fingertips.

Boots are steel-shank, oil-resistant, with mag-lock heel capability. All panels connect via quick-release buckles for field maintenance. The entire kit ships in a compressed carry-bag and assembles in under four minutes. Standard colorway is gunmetal with amber corponation stripe.
functionality: Full ballistic protection to Class 3, integrated neural HUD uplink, mag-lock boot heel for surface adhesion, quick-release panel system for field repair, thermal signature dampening on torso.
what_it_says: You are a sanctioned instrument of force — credentialed, equipped, and expendable.
story_hooks: A unit's loadout serial number traces back to a black-site requisition that officially never happened.
The HUD uplink has a firmware backdoor — someone is watching through every officer's visor.
A disgraced CorpSec officer still has her full kit; no one came to collect it after she was burned.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, militaristic full-body tactical ensemble that reads as corporate enforcement. Angular, segmented armor plating creates a geometric silhouette with pronounced shoulders and reinforced joints. The matte-black finish absorbs light, creating sharp definition between panels. Worn by mid-tier CorpSec operatives—confident, intimidating, professional.
physical_description.fit: Precision-tailored compression fit underneath modular armor segments. Torso hugs the body snugly; shoulder pauldrons flare slightly outward for protection and psychological impact. Knee greaves articulate with the leg without restricting movement. Overall silhouette is athletic and purposeful—built for combat-ready mobility.
physical_description.primary_material: Segmented TacShell composite (matte black) over graphene moisture-wicking underlayer; ceramic shoulder pauldrons; carbon composite helmet; syntex cut-resistant gloves; steel-shank oil-resistant boots
physical_description.texture: Matte, non-reflective surfaces on armor; finely ribbed graphene underlayer visible at articulation points; haptic nodes create subtle bumps on glove fingertips; steel toe and heel catch light distinctly
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal and matte black dominant; amber corponation stripe running vertically down center chest and along helmet ridge; occasional metallic silver at mag-locks and quick-release buckles
physical_description.closures: Quick-release magnetic buckles throughout; mag-lock heel system on boots; friction-fit helmet with neural port; friction-seal glove wrists
distinctive_features: Integrated HUD visor with neural uplink port at helmet occipital ridge
Segmented TacShell plating with visible seam lines for articulation
Haptic feedback nodes embedded in glove fingertips
Quick-release modular panel system for field maintenance
Mag-lock heel capability on boots for anchoring in high-G environments
Amber corponation stripe (Rheon Systems corporate branding)
Low-profile carbon composite helmet—sleek, not bulky
Ceramic shoulder pauldrons with distinctive angular geometry
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2 (mid-tier corporate issue)—expensive, standardized, mass-produced at scale for corpo security forces. Not luxury, not salvage.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this signals corporate enforcement authority, security clearance, and corpo loyalty. The wearer is muscle for a megacorp, trained and equipped, middle-management of violence. A walking statement of corporate jurisdiction.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when issued; broken-in after field deployment with minor scratches on armor panels, amber stripe slightly dulled, mag-locks occasionally sticky. Field operators maintain it meticulously—dirt accumulation in joint seams is a mark of negligence.
